climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 6°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

sheet.soil: Greenstone and clay over fractured limestone at Monte Bello.
sheet.elevation: Monte Bello vines sit from about 1,300 to 2,700 feet.

claims.claim: The Santa Cruz Mountains AVA was established in 1981.
The AVA boundary follows the coastal fog line. It sits near 400 feet on the Pacific side and 800 feet on the Bay side, and rises to about 3,000 feet at the ridge crests.
Soils across the AVA are mostly Franciscan shale, sandstone and clay, thin and stony.
At Monte Bello the soils are greenstone and clay over decomposing, fractured limestone.
Ridge says limestone is missing from the best-known Cabernet areas of Napa and Sonoma.
Monte Bello vines sit between about 1,300 and 2,700 feet.
The climate is cool. Ridge calls Monte Bello one of California's coolest Cabernet areas.
The AVA was drawn by topography, with a boundary set by elevation and fog.
The AVA is known for Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, each about a quarter of plantings.
Ridge says Monte Bello has often been called America's First Growth and is known for aging for decades.
Santa Cruz Mountains is a stand-alone appellation between the North Coast and the Central Coast, and part of neither.
